OSF u93eq's 'NAS - questionnaire and translations/NAS.xlsx' marks exactly four of its 16 rows with an asterisk and states 'Items marked with * were used in the within-person protocol': Abusive (row 1), Nasty (row 8), Exploitative (row 13), Depreciating (row 15). The Study 5 daily codebook lists those same four Polish adjectives under the heading NAS. The response format also differs from Studies 1-2: NAS.xlsx gives 'Within-person response scale: Visual analogue slider bar ranging from 0 (Not at all) to 100 (Extremely)', matching the live resp set 0-100, where Studies 1-2 were 1-7.

LANGUAGE -- Study 5 was administered in POLISH, unlike Studies 1 and 2 (Prolific, English). Both Study 5 codebooks are entirely in Polish, and the baseline codebook names the running institutions ('Akademii Ekonomiczno-Humanistycznej w Warszawie, Uniwersytetu Slaskiego w Katowicach, Instytutu Filozofii Polskiej Akademii Nauk'). Per the 2026-09-01 schema the administered Polish sits in item_text/instructions/option_text and the English in the _translated columns; language=Polish.

MAPPING IS PARTIAL, NOT VERIFIED -- 'Study 5 NAS.sav' carries NO variable labels and NO value labels (all 17 columns return None for both levels), so which Polish adjective NAS1..NAS4 holds is an ORDER inference off the study's own 'Study 5 Codebook - Daily.docx' (mapping_basis=paper_order). Two routes were run against live data (verify_nas_rogoza_2024_study5_nas.R, VERDICT: PASS): route 8 pins NAS2 = Lekceważący/Depreciating (mean 16.152 vs 12.431-12.932 for the rest, 47.27% at 0 vs 52.70-54.86%), and route 1 (cross-study nomological profile anchored on Study 2's batch_114-verified mapping) pins NAS3 = Wyzyskujący/Exploitative (lowest live NVS-minus-NGS differential, 0.183; Exploitative is the only one of the four whose Study 2 NGS correlation exceeds its NVS correlation, d = -0.073). NOT established: NAS1 vs NAS4, i.e. Znieważający/Abusive vs Bezczelny/Nasty -- their live means differ by 0.5 points on a 0-100 slider (12.923 vs 12.431) and their Study 2 anchors differ by 0.003 in d. If those two are swapped, nothing in the data would show it. A reader who needs NAS1/NAS4 disambiguated should treat them as an unordered pair.

RIVAL ORDERING TESTED AND REJECTED -- the plausible alternative is that the daily items follow the 16-item form's own order (Abusive, Nasty, Exploitative, Depreciating), not the daily codebook's (Abusive, Depreciating, Exploitative, Nasty). Over all 24 assignments the shipped one scores Spearman rho=0.80 against the Study 2 profile (rank 2 of 24, tied) and the NAS.xlsx ordering scores 0.40; under the rival, the mildest adjective (Depreciating) would be the least endorsed and most floored item, which is not what the data show.

ENGLISH PROVENANCE IS MIXED, and one field is IRW-authored. item_text_translated (Abusive / Depreciating / Exploitative / Nasty) and option_text_translated ('Not at all', 'Extremely') are the study's OWN English from NAS.xlsx. instructions_translated ('With reference to today's events, how well do these adjectives describe how you felt?') has no published English anywhere in the deposit -- the daily codebook exists in Polish only and NAS.xlsx carries only the trait-level instruction -- so it was translated by this project. translation_source=mixed; the machine-translated instruction is disclosed in public_note.

ANCHOR WORDING DIVERGES BETWEEN THE STUDY'S OWN TWO SOURCES. The Polish daily codebook prints '0 = w ogóle; 100 = całkowicie' (literally 'not at all' / 'completely'); NAS.xlsx renders the same within-person scale as '0 (Not at all) to 100 (Extremely)'. The study's own English is shipped in option_text_translated rather than a literal gloss of 'całkowicie'; the divergence is noted rather than silently reconciled. Points 1-99 are unlabelled on the slider and ship with option_text and option_text_translated BLANK -- they are not padded with their own numbers.

TRANSCRIPTION DEVIATIONS, all deliberate: (1) the codebook's 'Response Options: 0 = w ogóle; 100 = całkowicie' line was moved out of `instructions` into `option_text` rather than recorded twice; (2) the instruction is the codebook's single instruction for the consolidated NVS+NAS+NGS 12-adjective daily block, i.e. it is shared with the sibling study5_nvs and study5_ngs tables -- it is whole-table framing, so it sits in `instructions` with one trivial section_id and a blank section_prompt; (3) the daily codebook spells the second adjective 'Lekceważący' and the baseline codebook agrees, while NAS.xlsx spells it 'Lekceważacy' (missing the acute accent) -- the two-source spelling is shipped and the NAS.xlsx form treated as a typo.

CORROBORATION THAT THE LIVE TABLE IS THE .sav -- the authors' own Mplus output 'Multilevel CFA/CFA DD.out' reports per-variable sample sizes NAS1 8212, NAS2 8210, NAS3 8206, NAS4 8204, which equal the live IRW per-item n exactly (irw_table_sets, 38,040 rows total), and means 12.919/16.150/12.929/12.430 against live 12.923/16.152/12.932/12.431 (the tiny residual is the .out's listwise-ish treatment of the 9999 missing code, which data/nas_rogoza_2024.R converts to NA). This is plumbing, not mapping -- the .out uses the same NAS1..NAS4 codes -- but it rules out any drift between deposit and live table.

RIGHTS: NO BLOCK. The NAS is the source authors' own new instrument, published by them at https://osf.io/u93eq under CC0 1.0 Universal (verified via api.osf.io 2026-09-09: node license 'CC0 1.0 Universal'), including the dedicated 'NAS - questionnaire and translations/NAS.xlsx' giving the English, Polish and German forms. The only condition-shaped text in that file is 'Please cite as: Rogoza, R., Flakus, M., Baran, L., & Fatfouta, R. (2022). Development and validation of the Narcissistic Antagonism Scale.' -- a citation request, not a fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution term. No NAS row in itemtext/instrument_rights_register.csv. The APA article carries a personal-use notice, but that is a notice about the article, not a term governing the instrument, and none of the wording shipped here comes from the article.

Study 5 is a 30-day daily-diary (SEMA3) protocol administered in POLISH. The base text fields therefore carry the Polish wording from the study's own 'Study 5 Codebook - Daily.docx' (OSF u93eq, CC0 1.0) and the English sits in the four _translated columns, per the 2026-09-01 administered-language rule. item_text_translated and option_text_translated are the authors' own English, quoted from the article's Study 5 Measures paragraph ('the NGS (Brilliant, Glorious, Powerful, Prestigious)' and 'a visual analogue slider bar (0 = not at all to 100 = completely)'). instructions_translated is NOT the authors' -- no English rendering of the daily instruction exists anywhere in the deposit or the paper, so it was translated for this table by IRW. That is the only IRW-generated string in the file, and it is why translation_source is `mixed` rather than `study_supplied`.

Step 3b: the table name is right but the instrument is NOT the study's own new scale. This table holds the Narcissistic Grandiosity Scale (NGS; Crowe, Carter, Campbell & Miller, 2016), a comparison measure Rogoza et al. administered alongside their new NAS -- specifically the four-adjective daily state subset (Brilliant, Glorious, Powerful, Prestigious) taken from Edershile & Wright (2021), not the 13-item trait NGS the same study's baseline questionnaire used. The `instrument` field names it accordingly. Note the daily set is not a subset of the study's own trait NGS-13: Genialny/Brilliant is one of the three NGS-16 adjectives the Polish 13-item trait form drops.

The 0-100 visual analogue slider labels only its two endpoints (0 = w ogole / not at all, 100 = calkowicie / completely). option_text and option_text_translated are populated for resp=0 and resp=100 and left blank for 1-99; the 99 unlabelled points were NOT padded with their own numbers. The file is therefore 4 items x 101 resp levels = 404 rows, 396 of which carry blank option_text by design.

Mapping verification is PARTIAL, not clean (see verify_nas_rogoza_2024_study5_ngs.R). The 'Study 5 NAS.sav' carries no variable labels and no value labels at either level, so which adjective NGS1..NGS4 hold is an order inference. Two independent order sources agree -- the Study 5 daily codebook and the paper's own Measures paragraph, and the Study 6 state codebook repeats the identical four-adjective order -- and the data rule out the one rival ordering on record, but nothing distinguishes Brilliant from Glorious or Powerful from Prestigious. 8 of the 24 possible orderings survive the checks.

Caveat on the strength of one check: the two-block correlation test passes by a thin margin (min claimed within-pair r = 0.730 for NGS3-NGS4, max cross-pair r = 0.721 for NGS2-NGS3). The item-location check is what carries the block split cleanly (means 32.4/32.9 vs 24.5/23.4, floor 24.3%/23.0% vs 36.4%/39.0%), and the rival-ordering check is decisive against the Edershile & Wright listing order (its implied within-pair r 0.676/0.663 against a 0.814 cross-pair).

Step 5b status is PARTIAL, not VERIFIED. The Study 5 .sav has no variable or value labels, so codes NVS1..NVS4 are tied to adjectives only by presentation order -- but by three independent documents in the same deposit/paper that all give the same order (Study 5 daily codebook, Study 6 state codebook, and the article's Study 5 Measures sentence 'we used four items from the NVS (Ignored, Resentful, Misunderstood, Underappreciated)'). The data pin the block split only: person means NVS3 25.35 and NVS4 22.00 sit above NVS1 19.26 and NVS2 18.81 (all four paired contrasts p < 3e-6), matching the same authors' English Study 2 trait means where Misunderstood 3.105 and Underappreciated 3.334 sit above Ignored 2.629 and Resentful 2.252. They do not separate NVS1 from NVS2 (difference 0.45, p = 0.23), and NVS3 > NVS4 is the reverse of Study 2's rank for Misunderstood vs Underappreciated -- across a different sample, language, timeframe and response format, so it is not read as a contradiction, but the within-block order is unverified. See verify_nas_rogoza_2024_study5_nvs.R.

Item NVS1's Polish item_text is shipped verbatim as 'Zleckewazony', which is a misspelling of the Polish word 'Zlekcewazony' (spelled correctly for the same adjective in the same OSF deposit's Study 3 codebook). It was NOT corrected because both of the deposit's state-protocol codebooks -- Study 5 Daily and Study 6 State -- carry the same misspelling, so it may be what the SEMA3 app actually displayed.

The instrument's response scale is a 0-100 visual analogue slider that labels only its endpoints (0 = w ogole / not at all, 100 = calkowicie / completely). All 101 resp levels ship a row per item because respondents used the full range, and option_text is blank for 1..99 by design -- the unlabelled points were not padded with their own numbers. This will read as a large blank-option_text share in any batch audit; it is the expected shape.

translation_source=mixed, and one component is IRW-generated: the English adjectives and the English anchors are the authors' own (article Methods; deposit NAS.xlsx), but the English instruction line was translated by this project because the deposit publishes no English for the daily-diary instruction. A public issues-page entry is owed on that basis when the table goes live; a public_note is written.

Not a defect, recorded because the table name invites the wrong reading: the NVS is not these authors' instrument. It is the 11-adjective Narcissistic Vulnerability Scale of Crowe et al. (2018), Psychological Assessment 30(7):978-983, of which Study 5 administered four adjectives as a daily state measure. instrument is named accordingly.
